summary.headline: Juniper FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR1,047.7 crores and PAT nearly doubled to INR141.6 crores, with 42% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 posted record quarterly operating revenue of INR301.5 crores and EBITDA of INR138 crores at a 45% margin, the sixth consecutive PAT-positive quarter. Portfolio ARR grew 9% for FY26 while occupancy rose 1% to 75%, with Grand Hyatt Mumbai, Andaz Delhi and Hyatt Regency Ahmedabad beating their comp sets. Management said April ARR grew only 1-2% but May occupancy was tracking ahead of budget. The pipeline was expanded with a 500-key Delhi (Dwarka) award and Westin Bengaluru Phase 1 (238 keys) set to open in Q2 FY27, though the 2030 room target was cut to about 3,320 keys.

segments.name: Rooms (portfolio ARR and occupancy)
segments.commentary: Q4 portfolio ARR rose 8% YoY to INR13,457 with occupancy stable at 81%; FY26 ARR up 9% and occupancy up 1% to 75%. Grand Hyatt Mumbai ARR +6%, Andaz Delhi +7%, Hyatt Regency Ahmedabad +25% in Q4.

segments.name: Food and beverage
segments.commentary: Q4 F&B revenue INR84.8 crores, 28% of total revenue; events are 62.5% of F&B and drove margin gains. Grand Showroom revenue nearly doubled YoY in Q4 and contributed INR28 crores in FY26.

segments.name: Annuity assets (apartments and lease rentals)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR43 crores, +18% YoY, equal to 1.9x finance cost.

guidance_outlook: Westin Bengaluru Phase 1 (238 keys) expected to open in Q2 FY27; management declined to give a firmer month.

Bengaluru Westin first-year (FY27) revenue about INR30 crores; stabilised-year revenue about INR120 crores; ARR starting near INR15,000; stabilised EBITDA margin 40%+; stabilisation in 6-9 months, fully stabilised next year.
Bengaluru Phase 2 (266 keys, taking asset to 504 keys) expected to go into development in H2 FY27.
Capex about INR1,800 crores from now to FY30 for 1,400-plus keys; about INR300 crores in FY27 and INR700-750 crores in FY28.
Peak debt in FY28, still below the 2.5x debt-to-EBITDA target.
Q1 FY27 expected in line with management's expectations; H1 FY27 growth likely but may not be double-digit; H2 business seen as strong.
Portfolio target rises from 1,895 rooms in FY26 to over 3,320 keys by FY30 (over 1,400 additional rooms).
capex_capacity: Delhi Dwarka/Aerocity project: 500-key luxury hotel on 2.5 acres awarded by DDA on a 55-year lease; upfront payment about INR9.75 crores over 4 years; no lease payment during 5-year construction; annual license fee starts at about INR16 crores after 5.5 years, rising 5% p.a. for 8 years then 7%.
Bengaluru: Westin Phase 1 238 keys (Q2 FY27 opening); Phase 2 266 keys (H2 FY27 development start).
Kaziranga 106-key resort and Guwahati 315-key project continuing on plan.

Grand Hyatt Mumbai adjoining land: smaller parcel with about 80,000 sq ft potential; approvals expected around October, construction targeted before year-end. Larger parcel development strategy still being finalised.
demand_pricing: April 2026 portfolio ARR grew 1-2% YoY after a soft start; May occupancy month-to-date up about 10 bps YoY and tracking ahead of budget.
Demand is mainly domestic business travel; foreign travellers about 25-30% of mix, largely airline crew in Delhi and Mumbai.
Management said March-April business was pushed out rather than lost, and H1 is seasonally softer than H2.
Aerocity micro-market at 82-85% occupancy with high rates; Bengaluru micro-market rates above INR15,000 (Taj and Moxy are competitors).
Management expects Delhi demand CAGR of about double digits against supply CAGR of 5-6%; Bengaluru demand double digits against supply 6-6.5%.
Grand Hyatt Mumbai occupancy around 76%; management sees a few points of headroom plus about INR2,000 of rate upside.
Ahmedabad transient ARR +28% vs comp set +16% in Q4; positioned as a luxury asset with 270 rooms.
Management said Mumbai's Grand Showroom has at least 25-30% further upside.

qa_highlights.question: What are April and May trends given West Asia-related travel disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: April was soft, with portfolio ARR up 1-2%; May occupancy is up about 10 bps YoY month-to-date and tracking ahead of budget. Management said the disruption is now baseline.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Westin chosen over JW or Grand Hyatt for Bengaluru, and when does it open?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Westin is a luxury brand for the location, with Marriott approvals in place, and opening is guided only to Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Delhi DDA lease terms and the scope for expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease is 55 years; upfront INR9.75 crores paid over 4 years; license fee from about year 5.5 at about INR16 crores. No further expansion is possible beyond 500 keys.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bengaluru Westin revenue and margin ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue about INR30 crores; stabilised revenue about INR120 crores (Phase 1); stabilised EBITDA margin 40%+; full stabilisation next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex profile and peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,800 crores to FY30; INR300 crores in FY27 and INR700-750 crores in FY28. Debt peaks in FY28, below 2.5x debt-to-EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the room target fall from about 4,000 by FY29 to 3,320 by FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure reflects only firmed-up projects (about 3,200 rooms confirmed); it remains a growth-focused company and will pursue further additions.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 growth is tracking in line but April was soft; H1 may not be double-digit, and the outlook depends on the geopolitical situation not escalating.
Execution risk: the room target was cut from about 4,000 (by FY29, per prior annual report) to 3,320 (by FY30); investors questioned guidance credibility.
Bengaluru opening is only guided as Q2 FY27 and the brand is new to the market; ramp assumptions (INR30 crores in year 1, INR120 crores stabilised) need tracking.
Delhi micro-market supply additions (ITC at Yashobhoomi and others) could pressure ARR.
ROFO and brownfield acquisitions remain undisclosed; any non-cash acquisition would be a governance and valuation watch item.
Past property tax liability (INR23 crores for Andaz Delhi) may apply to all Delhi assets under the high court judgment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the pipeline, with a clear emphasis on return discipline. Management was evasive on ROFO asset details, the Bengaluru opening month, brownfield deal size, and the reasons for the lower room target, and deferred market-cap questions to investors.
key_quotes: Juniper closed FY26 on a strong note by achieving another record quarter with revenue of INR306.8 crores in Q4FY26.
I'm happy to note that we have achieved our stated goal of achieving EBITDA margins in excess of 40%, which we set out at the start of the year.
So, we believe there is at least 25% to 30% further upside on that.
There would be no further expansion possible on that asset.
